title: Before you buy a trading bot: I stress-tested a $900 gold EA with 3 simple tests. It passed one and failed two.
author: Large_Front_4291
selftext:
A lot of people here ask whether trading bots are worth it. I tested a popular gold EA from the MQL5 Market (My AI Gold, v1.82, $899.95) without buying it: everything below uses its free demo in the MT5 Strategy Tester, on custom symbols built from real broker prices (0.10 fixed lots).

\*\*Its own history looks great:\*\* profit factor about 1.7-2.5 on XAUUSD 2016-2026.

\*\*Three stress tests:\*\*

|Test|EA profit factor|Random entries|  
|:-|:-|:-|  
|Disguised year: 2015 data relabelled as 2016 (it never trades 2015)|2.10 (passed)|0.92|  
|Twin market: gold priced in euro (hourly moves 0.84 correlated with XAUUSD)|1.09 (failed)|0.96|  
|Shuffled days (3 versions)|0.89-1.17 (failed)|\\\~1.0|  
|Shuffled weeks (control)|2.38|\\\~1.0|

The twin market is the telling one: on gold priced in euro, which moves almost like gold in dollars, the edge disappears. Small changes in the price path flip most of its decisions. Our run on the last six months (June-November 2026) gave PF 1.06.

\*\*Takeaway for anyone shopping for a bot:\*\* a great backtest only shows how it did on the prices it was built on. Before paying, test it on data it hasn't seen and compare it with random entries using the same stops and targets.

No affiliation with the developer, no affiliate links, not investment advice.

Have you ever bought a bot that kept its backtest edge live? What do you check before paying?

comments.author: AlgoTradingQuant
comments.body: I build my own using Python + broker API but I spent years backtesting thousands of strategies and automated the ones that had real edge

replies.author: Large_Front_4291
replies.body: When you tested thousands of strategies, how did you tell which ones had a real edge and which ones just got lucky in the backtest? Did their performance hold up once you traded them live?

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body: The twin market test is a clever one. I'd also try wider spreads and more slippage than the demo gives, small edges often disappear there.

replies.author: Large_Front_4291
replies.body: Thanks, good point. I used broker prices, but I haven’t tested wider spreads or extra slippage yet. I’d start with the June–November XAUUSD run since the profit factor was only 1.06. I’d keep the EA settings fixed, widen the spread first, then test slippage separately and finally combine them. What I’d really like to know is how much worse execution has to get before the profit factor drops below 1.
